title: Atomized ChargeSmith panel — token-level attribution & export UX
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Overview: Design a compact, composable panel (ChargeSmith) for the Redwood Console that surfaces atomized token-level charge details, flexible attribution views, and an export workflow. Goal: let engineers and finance users quickly understand why a given route/model incured cost, reconcile anomalous spend, and export row-level charge data for billing or chargeback. Scope includes an embeddable panel for dashboards, an expanded detail drawer, microcopy for pricing terms, CSV/JSON export schema, and price-band hints for common quantization/batching profiles. This ticket covers prototype screens, interaction specs, and handoff artifacts for engineering and PM review.

Key UX problems addressed: 
- Lack of row-level transparency in per-route spend views.
- Difficulty attributing cost to prompt vs. assistant vs. tool calls.
- No first-class export schema for downstream chargeback systems.

User personas: 
- Platform engineer reconciling a spike in cost after a model rollout.
- Product analyst building a chargeback report for a product team.
- Finance partner auditing monthly invoice line items.

Edge cases considered: 
- Mixed-model rollouts (one request uses encoder from model A and decoder from model B).
- Cached prefix tokens (charged separately vs. aggregated depending on SLO).
- Partial attribution when prompts include third-party tool calls.

Design constraints: 
- Keep panel height < 420px when used in dashboard card.
- Use current Console design tokens and table component to avoid extra engineering cost.
- Export file must contain deterministic keys to map back to request logs (request_id, timestamp, route, model_hash, prompt_slice_id).
acceptance_criteria: Prototype Figma screens for Dashboard card + Detail drawer accepted by PM and Eng
Export schema documented and sample CSV/JSON generated for review
Micro-interactions (hover tooltip, row expand, attribution breakdown) detailed in specs
Accessibility: contrast and keyboard navigation passes internal a11y checklist
Handoff notes with clear API surface for ENG-28942 including required fields and example payload
decisions: Show both aggregated per-request cost and decomposed per-token cost in same row; allow toggle to expand tokens
Default attribution buckets: Prompt, Assistant (system), Tools, KV-cache hits, Network overhead
Export schema will include a flattened 'cost_breakdown' JSON string column in CSV to keep row schema stable
Price hints: show derived USD cost using current customer price tier plus per-token rate breakdown as micro-copy
review_comments: 2026-03-11 — Arjun Patel (ENG): Request example payload format for sequence-level vs. token-level charges. Need request_id, model_hash, tokens_in, tokens_out, kv_cache_saved_tokens. Also flagged performance risk of expanding all tokens in large batches (we should limit expansion to first 200 tokens by default).
2026-03-11 — Priya Singh (PM): Love the attribution buckets. Ask: include a 'confidence' flag for attribution heuristics when we guess which prompt fragment caused the majority of tokens?

2026-03-12 — Leah O'Connor (Design reviewer): Improve visual separation between aggregated cost and per-token detail. Suggest using a subtle divider + collapsible rows to avoid UX clutter. Also suggested updating microcopy to define 'KV-cache hits' for non-technical finance reviewers.

Iterate Figma to show collapsed-by-default large requests + 'show all tokens' affordance — due 2026-03-15
Schedule joint review with PM, ENG, and Security for export schema and PII review (security_review_required=true) — meeting 2026-03-16
